workingTitle: Euclid finds that faint intracluster light traces dark halo shapes
publicationStatus: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics; preprint submitted October 21, 2026.
coreFacts: The Euclid Collaboration analysed diffuse intracluster light in 205 clusters selected from eROSITA and Dark Energy Survey catalogues, spanning redshifts 0.1 to 0.8 and halo masses from 10^14 to about 10^15.2 solar masses.
Robust intracluster-light position angles and ellipticities at about 0.1 times the cluster radius, typically near 100 kiloparsecs, were measured for 130 clusters, or 63 percent of the sample.
The projected ellipticity distribution peaks near 0.5, consistent with independent strong- and weak-lensing estimates of cluster halo shapes.
The central brightest galaxy is relatively round, with ellipticity around 0.15 to 0.20, while the surrounding diffuse light becomes more elongated and reaches about 0.5 near 0.1 cluster radii.

Eighty-seven percent of robust intracluster-light measurements align within 30 degrees of the brightest cluster galaxy; satellite-galaxy orientations meet that threshold for 61 percent of their smaller robust subset.
Stacking 163 clusters extends the diffuse-light detection to 0.6 to 0.8 cluster radii and shape measurements to 0.3 to 0.4 cluster radii.
caveats: Intracluster light is a luminous proxy for the dark-matter potential, not a direct image of dark matter.
Only 63 percent of the full sample yielded robust shapes at the comparison radius, while satellite-galaxy orientations were robust for only 30 percent.
Line-of-sight projection, cluster selection, mass, dynamical state, residual masking, and background treatment can bias apparent ellipticity.
The current sample is too small to separate all dependencies on selection, mass, and dynamical state; the authors defer that work to Euclid DR1.
Stacked profiles are slightly rounder than individual clusters because residual orientation differences and isophotal twists dilute ellipticity.
sourceStatus: Full accepted Astronomy & Astrophysics paper read, including sample construction, image processing, shape extraction, simulations, lensing comparison, alignment analysis, stacking, caveats, and conclusions. The primary paper directly supports all material claims; separate corroboration was unnecessary.
